outlook.statement: The company might explore and expand these activities further as and when opportunities arise in the future within the scope of its objects as per the Memorandum of Association.

Statements in these reports describing company's projections statements, expectations and hopes are forward looking. Though, these expectations are based on reasonable assumptions, the actual results might differ. Several factors could make a significant difference to the Company's operations. These include economic conditions, government regulations, taxation, natural calamity and currency rate changes, among others over which the Company does not have any direct control.
The Company's foray into trading of steel products in international market shall of course be subject to the overall demand stabilising in the world market, which looks promising.
The trading in Iron & steel products, including engineering products, in the international market is expected to continued.

risks: Continued blockades at the Strait of Hormuz, shortages of fuel and elevated energy costs are a key risk to the Indian economy.

Given its import reliance, India risks a widening current account deficit, pressure on public finances, consequent tightening in fiscal spend, higher than anticipated consumer inflation and eventual demand erosion, if the blockade continues.

The Company is involved in proceedings before the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) / National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) arising from petitions filed by M/s. M.B. Gupta HUF and others (C.P. No.(IB) 347/CHE/2020) and Mr. Suresh Kumar Jalan and others (C.P. 38/CHE/2023), both of which represent re-litigation of matters previously dismissed across multiple forums including the erstwhile Company Law Board, the Hon'ble High Court of Madras, and the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.

The Hon'ble NCLT, Chennai allowed the Company's maintainability application (IA (IBC) 1177(CHE)/2020) vide order dated 18th September 2025 in C.P. No. (IB) 347/CHE/2020. M/s. M.B. Gupta HUF and others have filed an appeal against the said order before the NCLAT, Chennai, which has been marked defect-free on 16th May 2026 and is pending for directions.

The application filed by Mr. Suresh Kumar Jalan and others seeking transfer of C.P. No. 38/CHE/2023 from NCLT, Chennai to another bench (TA (C. Act)- 10(PB)/2026 before NCLT, New Delhi, Principal Bench) has been dismissed vide order dated 20th May 2026, being devoid of merit. C.P. No. 38/CHE/2023 accordingly remains pending before NCLT, Chennai.
